I don't know much about this, what's wrong with X11 and why are they trying to get away from it?

X is old, really old. New solutions may use the innovations of the past few decades. The client-server model which X uses is no longer looked as the way to go for graphics. Also X handles input from keyboard and mice but for example no audio output.
It might be old, but it is something that works flawlessly and (as of today) has no other replacement. Even after Wayland or Mir come out of development, they will take a long while to get stability.
True. But even if the reincarnation hasn't all the cool features like X over SSH and X2X, sometimes software projects need to face time, drop support for outdated systems and support the new ones.
Why should a windowing system handle audio output? I can imagine many cases where you'd want a headless computer capable of playing audio.

It's one of the outputs which are normally per session. It would make remote desktop better if not every product would have to reinvent the wheel. Also multihead setups. I see why there still is need for audio without running a running full blown X and Linux audio is a whole mess by itself. But when you have a windowing system handling keyboards, mice, joysticks and displays, why not include audio input and output as well?

The biggest reason for dumping X are basically that it's big and bulky and most applications just use it for basic window functions and dealing with OpenGL contexts. They almost universally do their drawing with other mechanisms and then paint it onto the window; the drawing mechanisms of the X server go unused. Once X shipped drivers, now it uses drivers in the kernel(but has to do so via the old driver interface). Anything that uses indirect OpenGL can't use a version above 1.4 and most applications are beyond broken for the client-server model of X to begin with.

So, essentially, these projects are an outgrowth of the fact that most of X is legacy code and aim to replicate how modern programs actually work. If there were a serious argument about X's maintainability, they'd be wholly necessary, but so far every time the X server has run into some wall for modern programs, it's grown an extension to break through it. I'm not sure they actually any real problem.
